text:
Carla (CS): FYI Riverbend renewal: they're switching from CC to PO, want KMS enabled during onboarding, and want the contract signed by two different orgs (Purchasing + Security). Can we map procurement path and signature flow?
Mohit (AE): Meeting with their procurement tomorrow. They're asking if we can do Net30, 12-month term but bill per-quarter. Pricing won't change but need PO vendor code and a fixed SOW for KMS scope.
Daisy (Finance): Vendor code + tax id required. Also need billing entity confirmation (US vs EU). If they want Net30 we need an approved credit check — do we have that on file?
Ben (Legal): I need the final SOW and list of signers with titles. If two signatures across teams, we either route both in DocuSign or accept one E-Sign and one wet signature depending on their internal policy. Send me the draft.
Carla (CS): Attaching the draft SOW in docs link: https://docsend.example.com/riverbend-sow (will update after morning call).
daisy (Finance): +1 on credit check — I can run it Monday if Mohit shares the legal name and billing address.
Tim (EngOps): KMS onboarding note: for Private we need 3–4 weeks to provision and validate key syncs. For Hosted we can offer a customer-managed key via our hosted KMS integration but it has policy constraints (no HSM export). Which path do they prefer?
Mohit (AE): They want the key to live in their cloud (HSM) ideally. They asked if we can accept a delay and start with a temporary scoped key to unblock training and early enablement.
Ben (Legal): Temporary key is fine but must be written into SOW (scope + retention + revocation). Also need SOC and encryption notes for procurement folks.
Carla (CS): Riverbend's procurement lead said they can issue a PO but need Redwood's vendor code and our W9. Daisy, can you share vendor code and W9 link?
Daisy (Finance): Vendor code: RW-51423. W9 link: https://internal.example.com/w9/redwood.pdf. Sending to Mohit via DM.
Mohit (AE): Great. I'll confirm PO template with them. Quick Q: can we accept staged signing? e.g., Purchasing signs PO first, Security signs SOW after KMS review?
Ben (Legal): Yes, staged signing is acceptable if the contract includes a clause that makes SOW effective only after both signers complete execution. I'll add a conditional effectiveness clause.
Tim (EngOps): Operationally: if they sign PO now but KMS later, we should gate KMS features until key rotation completes. We can enable non-sensitive features earlier. Need an enablement checklist for the CS onboarding playbook.
Carla (CS): I'll prepare a staggered enablement plan: week 0 — contract & PO accepted; week 1 — baseline onboarding (non-KMS features); week 3–5 — KMS provisioning and security review; week 6 — full production access. Any objections?
Ben (Legal): Sounds good. Add an explicit rollback/termination right if they fail security attestation within X days.
Daisy (Finance): Confirming Net30 — finance will accept PO with that term once credit check clears.
Mohit (AE): I'll push procurement to issue PO tomorrow; will ask for the exact signer names and whether they require wet signature for security sign-off.
Carla (CS): Action items: Mohit to get PO + signer names by EOD tomorrow; Daisy to run credit check and send vendor docs; Ben to update SOW + conditional effectiveness clause; Tim to draft KMS onboarding checklist; I'll produce the staggered enablement timeline and share with Riverbend.
deploy-bot: Task created: #RB-RENEW-4521 assigned to Carla, Mohit, Daisy, Ben, Tim — due 2026-03-28.
Mohit (AE): Noted. I'll ping here after procurement call. :thumbsup: 
Carla (CS): Thanks team — please drop any docs/responses into this thread so I can keep Riverbend updated in the same place. :calendar:
